sentenceSets.sentence: The traditional dichotomy between science and the humanities obscures how much each has borrowed from the other.

answerChoices.reasoning: Distinction describes a difference or contrast; while there is a distinction between science and humanities, the sentence emphasizes their division into two opposed camps rather than just a difference.
Divide describes separation; while they are divided, dichotomy specifically emphasizes division into two mutually exclusive parts rather than just any separation.
Separation describes being apart; while they are separate, dichotomy more specifically emphasizes division into two opposed, mutually exclusive categories.
Opposition describes conflict or contrary positions; while science and humanities may oppose, dichotomy emphasizes the artificial division into two parts rather than active opposition.
Difference describes how things are not the same; while there are differences, the sentence emphasizes the specific structure of two opposed camps rather than just differences.
Conflict describes disagreement or struggle; the sentence shows division into two parts, not necessarily active conflict.
Gap describes a space or difference; while there is a gap, dichotomy emphasizes systematic division into two parts rather than just a gap.
Chasm describes a deep gap or divide; while the separation is dramatic, dichotomy emphasizes the specific structure of two mutually exclusive parts.
Similarity describes how things are alike; the sentence describes division and separation, opposite to similarity.
Unity describes coming together as one; the sentence shows division into two opposed camps.
Integration describes combining into a whole; the sentence shows division, opposite to integration.

sentenceSets.sentence: The dichotomy between private ambition and public service left the politician constantly torn between conflicting loyalties.

answerChoices.reasoning: Tension describes strain or stress between opposing forces; while there is tension, dichotomy more specifically emphasizes division into two mutually exclusive parts rather than just stress.
Conflict describes disagreement or struggle; the sentence shows internal struggle, but dichotomy emphasizes the structural division into two opposed categories.
Struggle describes difficult effort; while the politician struggles, dichotomy emphasizes the structural division into two opposed commitments rather than general struggle.
Dilemma describes a situation requiring difficult choice; while he faces a dilemma, dichotomy emphasizes the division into two opposed parts rather than the difficulty of choosing.
Opposition describes opposing forces; while his ambitions oppose, dichotomy emphasizes the structural division into two parts more than opposition as such.
Clash describes collision or strong disagreement; while his commitments clash, dichotomy emphasizes the division into two parts rather than the collision.
Incompatibility describes inability to coexist; while the commitments are incompatible, dichotomy emphasizes the systematic division into two rather than just inability to coexist.
Contradiction describes opposing statements or things; while the commitments contradict, dichotomy emphasizes the division into two mutually exclusive parts.
Harmony describes agreeing or combining well; the sentence describes division and conflict.
Alignment describes coming into agreement; the sentence shows opposed loyalties.
Synthesis describes combining into a whole; the sentence shows division into two opposed parts.

sentenceSets.sentence: The dichotomy between theory and practice proved illusory when researchers discovered that theoretical models often failed in real-world conditions.

answerChoices.reasoning: Distinction describes a difference; while there is a distinction, the sentence emphasizes the systematic division into two opposed categories rather than just a difference.
Separation describes being apart; while theory and practice are separate, dichotomy emphasizes their division as mutually exclusive categories.
Divide describes a split; while they are divided, dichotomy more specifically emphasizes the division into two opposed, mutually exclusive parts.
Gap describes a space between things; while there is a gap, dichotomy emphasizes the systematic division into two opposed categories rather than just a gap.
Difference describes how things are not the same; while they differ, dichotomy emphasizes the specific structure of two mutually exclusive parts.
Rift describes a serious break or divide; while applicable, it emphasizes dramatic separation rather than the systematic division into two parts.
Disparity describes inequality or difference; while there is disparity, dichotomy emphasizes the division into two opposed parts rather than just difference.
Schism describes a division or split, especially in an organization; while applicable, it suggests organizational division more than abstract division into two categories.
Unity describes coming together as one; the sentence describes division, later revealed as false.
Continuity describes uninterrupted connection; the sentence emphasizes separation between theory and practice.
Integration describes combining into a whole; the sentence shows division into two separate domains.
